//Aurora: The aurora itself: a self-timed hidden stat, the vanilla GarlicEffect shape, built exactly like the blood moon timer (Documentation/Research/HarshWilds/events_sky.md sections 5 and 7, the aurora DECISIONS). Written ONLY by the Aurora collection of SelfTriggeredAction/Tgr_HW_AuroraRoll.json (+HW_AURORA_TICKS = 40, its max, applied Permanent by ActionRoutine when that collection is picked), then it counts itself down at BaseRatePerTick -1 and rests at 0, so the aurora ends by itself after 40 ticks (ten hours) with no clearing code. While it reads 1 to 40 its one status is active: it raises a Moderate alert when the aurora begins (NotifyPlayer 2 NotifyWhenGoingUp, AlertLevel 2 Moderate) and shows the vanilla sprite Star in the status strip (Visibility 0 VisibleWithStatus and StatusesHaveNoBar true, as the blood moon timer; Visibility 2 would be NeverVisible and hide the alert). The status has NO EffectsOnStats on purpose: a status effect is a GlobalModifier on the whole run, and the aurora lifts mood only OUTSIDE under the open night sky. That is done by the second STA, SelfTriggeredAction/Tgr_HW_AuroraGlow.json, which reads this stat as a StatChangeTrigger entry {1,40} beside vanilla IsNightUnderOpenSky {1,1} and writes vanilla Morale a small step each tick; this stat is its timer and nothing more. It is a GLOBAL stat, so the alert shows wherever the player is, indoors too, while the mood step waits for the open sky (the timer keeps running: an aurora seen from a cabin is spent). HW_AURORA_TICKS = 40 (MinMaxValue.y, the status's ValueRange.y, the arm in Tgr_HW_AuroraRoll and the top of the glow's trigger range) is a TUNABLE PLACEHOLDER, session-inferred and unmeasured against play; the status text says 'up to ten hours', so retune it together with the text. INFERRED, harness probe: that the collection-level StatWarpData resolves in a mod STA (measured working for hw_stat_drought on 2026-09-30) and that a save reloaded mid-aurora keeps the stat.

Description.DefaultText: An aurora: standing under the open night sky lifts your mood.
An aurora is out tonight. Standing outside under the open night sky lifts your mood a little every quarter hour, for up to ten hours.
